instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave the lid on.

Peel the potatoes and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Cut the zucchini into half-moons, slice the onion, cut the tofu into 1-inch cubes, slice the scallions and mince the garlic. Cut the pork into 1-inch pieces.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high. Add the pork and the salt. Cook for 4 minutes, until it's browned in spots.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the gochujang and 1 tbsp of the gochugaru, and cook for 1 minute, stirring so it doesn't burn.
Add 5 cups of water and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot. Add the potatoes, turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil, then simmer for 6 minutes.
Add the onion, zucchini, soy sauce and sugar. Simmer for 4 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when you poke them.
Add the tofu, garlic and most of the scallions. Simmer for 2 minutes, then season with the pepper.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Put the remaining 1 tbsp gochugaru in a small bowl for the adults to stir in at the table. Top the stew with the last of the scallions and serve with the rice.
method_notes: The lead is Jongwon Baek's Pork Gochujang Jjigae on 10000recipe (4.79, linked to 39 reviews): pork browned, gochujang stirred in, then water, vegetables, gochugaru, soy sauce, garlic and tofu. Gangnam Kitchen's pork and potato stew agrees on pork, potato and a gochujang and gochugaru base. The lead leaves the potato out, so the potato and its cooking time come from Gangnam Kitchen and a second 10000recipe stew. Only 1 tbsp of the gochugaru goes in the pot and the rest goes on the table to keep the base mild. Honest time is a little over 30 minutes.
